claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous fcc matrix.
Gentle vacuum pre-annealing removes the native oxide layers from the alloy.
Degradation during elevated-temperature gas exposure is governed by the formation and stability of a dual-layer oxide scale.
The proposed dual-layer oxide scale consists primarily of Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
Under sufficiently oxidizing conditions, Al and Cr selectively oxidize synergistically.
Selective oxidation of Al and Cr produces a compact, continuous, and adherent protective oxide scale.
The continuous Al- and Cr-rich oxide scale passivates the surface and slows degradation.
Lower oxygen chemical potential disrupts formation of a cohesive protective oxide layer.
Oxide formed under reducing conditions accumulates stress and is prone to local spallation.
Scale spallation exposes the substrate to further degradation and accelerates degradation.
Oxidizing exposure between 700°C and 900°C will produce a well-formed continuous dual-layer oxide scale.
The scale formed under oxidizing conditions will exhibit lower in situ stress than scales formed under reducing conditions.
Oxidizing exposure will result in minimal degradation and preserved microstructural integrity.
Reducing exposure will produce a less continuous oxide scale with higher localized stress signatures.
Reducing exposure will ultimately cause scale spallation and faster degradation than oxidizing exposure.
Established oxidation kinetics support selective oxidation of Al and Cr.
